reader: source-only reader (publisher pictures + page facts); no analyzer, solver or model output was run or seen
frontHow: The ground plan marks the entrance with a black arrow at the bottom edge, pointing at the door of room 1.1 under the porch 1.6; the front elevation shows that door under a gabled porch between two windows.

overall.includes: The plain rectangular walled outline only. A further 105 is printed for the open entrance porch (1.6) in front; the side terrace (1.7) is not dimensioned. Neither is included.

outlineNote: One plain rectangle 8.55 x 7.05 with an open gabled entrance porch at the middle of the front and an open terrace on the right side.

bodies.name: entrance porch
bodies.position: open porch on two posts at the middle of the front wall, over the entrance door

uncertain: Page text gives 'Wysokosc kalenicy 7,09 m'; the section prints ridge +6,79 and terrain -0,30, so the page figure is the ridge above terrain and is used as the building height.

Rear dormer kind: the section and the attic plan put its window wall in the plane of the rear wall (so WALL), but on the rear elevation a strip of roof with an unbroken eaves line runs below the window, so it looks like a dormer standing on the slope; ROOF would also be defensible.

Rear dormer position: read from the rear elevation ([0.34, 0.60] incl. cheeks, slightly left of centre seen from the rear); the stair window on the attic plan sits slightly left of centre seen from the FRONT, which mirrored would give about [0.40, 0.66]. The two sources disagree by about 0.5 m.
The paired casement in the rear dormer is counted as one upper opening; each gable has one upper window.
The entrance porch gable is an open roof on posts, not a dormer; the front slope has no dormer and no roof window.
